nodes.description: A patent document titled "Real-time ad-hoc spam filtering of email" describing a multi-pass ad-hoc spam message filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier.

nodes.entity_id: Multi-Pass Ad-Hoc Spam Message Filtering Approach
nodes.description: A filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier during a first pass based on results of a previously applied message filter that sorts messages into folders, then uses the classifier in a second pass to retrospectively inspect messages and present potentially misclassified messages to the user.
nodes.id: Multi-Pass Ad-Hoc Spam Message Filtering Approach

nodes.description: A message filter that assigns messages to different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store; it is automatically executed independent of a user action.<SEP>A message filter that previously sorts messages into a plurality of different message folders and is configured to store first classification data in a persistent store.

A multi-pass message filter configured to generate a classification model based on a first pass analysis, perform a second pass to generate misclassification identification, and employ a Naive Bayes classifier.
A model generated by the multi-pass message filter based on first pass analysis, configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory location and purged after use.
Classification data generated by the first message filter and stored in a persistent store.<SEP>Classification data stored in a persistent store by the first message filter.

Classification data generated by the first pass of the multi-pass message filter to train the filter; it resides exclusively in a non-persistent memory store at the client device and is deleted upon providing the display of information.<SEP>Classification data generated by training the multi-pass message filter, configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory store and deleted after use.

A device configured to receive messages, assign them to different message folders using the first message filter, and communicate the messages over the network to the message folders.<SEP>A device comprising a transceiver to send and receive data over a network and a processor operative to perform first and second pass analyses, display misclassification identification, and purge the classification model from non-persistent memory.

A device that executes the multi-pass message filter, generates and stores second classification data in non-persistent memory, scores messages, identifies incorrectly sorted messages, and provides a display of information enabling a user to move messages to another folder.<SEP>A user's device on which the classification model is maintained in memory and on which the first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter may execute entirely.
A medium including data and instructions whose execution on a computing device provides for managing messages.
A plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted by the first message filter and to which misclassified messages can be moved.
Email messages that are sorted into folders, scanned for sender information, headers, subject, originating network address, contents, and attachments, and scored by the multi-pass message filter.
A classifier employed by the multi-pass message filter.
An identification of sorted messages that might be misclassified, generated by the second pass and displayed to the user.
A memory-resident-only location where the classification model resides, not stored on disk or another persistent data store.
A storage location where the first message filter stores first classification data.<SEP>A data store in which the first message filter stores first classification data.

A person enabled to move an identified message to another message folder, who may select the multi-pass message filter for execution through an interface on the client device.<SEP>A person whose mail folders are scanned and who is presented a list of potentially misclassified messages and enabled to move identified messages to another folder.

An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders; a message sender's address in the address book may be analyzed to generate second classification data.<SEP>An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders, used in analysis for generating the classification model.
Information about the sender read from messages during the first pass.
Message headers including a subject, read during the first pass.
Attachments within messages read during the first pass.

An interface on the client device through which a user may select the multi-pass message filter for execution.<SEP>An interface on the client device through which a user can select the multi-pass message filter for execution.

A message filter executed in multiple passes on sorted messages; a first pass trains the filter by generating second classification data, and a second pass uses that data to score each message and identify messages sorted into incorrect message folders.
A folder to which messages are assigned; messages may be sorted into an incorrect message folder and a user may move an identified message to another message folder.
A communication item received in plurality, assigned to message folders, scored by the multi-pass message filter, and potentially identified as stored in an incorrect message folder.
A memory store at the client device where the second classification data resides exclusively.
A communications network over which messages are communicated between the network device and the client device.
